# 1.3 Two pointers and sliding window

Phase 1 (Array techniques), target rating 1000–1400. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Shrinkable window (`shrinkable-window`)

Longest or shortest contiguous segment where validity is closed under shrinking.

**Works because:** If [l, r] is valid, every sub-window of it is valid.

### Fixed-size window (`fixed-window`)

Every window of length exactly k; update the window's value incrementally as it slides.

**Works because:** The window's value can be updated in O(1) or O(log n) when one element enters and one leaves.

### Count valid windows (`count-windows`)

Count segments satisfying a monotone condition by counting the valid windows that end at each r.

**Works because:** Validity is closed under shrinking, so for a fixed r the valid left ends form a range and contribute r − l + 1.

### Opposite ends of a sorted array (`opposite-ends`)

Pairs with a target sum or difference after sorting; the pointers move toward each other.

**Works because:** Sorted order makes the pair condition monotone in each pointer.

### Walk two sorted sequences (`merge-walk`)

Walk two sorted arrays together to merge them, match elements, or count pairs across them.

**Works because:** Both sequences are sorted, so once an element is passed it is never needed again and each pointer moves forward only.
